lead.question: 伊丽莎白为甩开纠缠不休的奈杰尔编了什么理由？结果如何？
lead.warmup: 你在街上看见一个“最不想见的人”，会立刻躲开吗？伊丽莎白正是如此：她穿过马路想避开奈杰尔·戴克斯，却被对方一眼瞧见、跑着迎了上来。奈杰尔永远无事可做，不管你多忙他都要跟着；伊丽莎白只好编个“去看牙医”的借口，没想到一句“候诊室里总有东西可读”就让计划落空。
goals: 掌握 avoid、enjoy、fancy、mind、finish 等动词后只接动名词的用法
掌握 It is no use doing、insist on doing、prevent sb. from doing、be busy doing 等含动名词的固定结构
会用 no matter + 疑问词引导让步状语从句
理解动名词的逻辑主语（my coming）
lead.summary: 伊丽莎白为避开奈杰尔穿过马路，却被一眼看见，装作没看见已无济于事，只好挥手。奈杰尔永远无事可做，不管人多忙都要跟着；她情急谎称去看牙医，对方却答“候诊室里总有东西可读”，照样跟了上来。全文几乎句句带动名词，是动名词用法的集中演练。
lead.tips: avoid、enjoy、fancy、mind、finish、insist on、it is no use、be busy、prevent sb. from 之后一律接动名词。

questions.q: Why did Elizabeth tell Nigel that she was going to the dentist?
questions.zh: 伊丽莎白为什么告诉奈杰尔她要去看牙医？
questions.a: She lied. She just wanted a way of preventing him from following her around all morning, so the dentist was only an excuse.
questions.aZh: 她在撒谎：只是想找个办法不让奈杰尔整个上午缠着她，“看牙医”是个借口。
questions.hint: 见 I had to think of a way of preventing him from following me around all morning。

questions.q: What did Elizabeth do when she saw Nigel, and why did she wave to him in the end?
questions.zh: 伊丽莎白看到奈杰尔时做了什么？为什么最后还是挥手？
questions.a: She crossed the street to avoid meeting him, but he saw her and came running towards her; it was no use pretending that she had not seen him, so she waved to him.
questions.aZh: 她穿过马路想避开他，可奈杰尔看见了她并朝她跑过来；再装作没看见已没有用，她只好挥手。

questions.q: Which sentence best describes Nigel's character? Quote it.
questions.zh: 课文中哪句话最能概括奈杰尔的性格？
questions.a: He never has anything to do. No matter how busy you are, he always insists on coming with you.
questions.aZh: 他从来都是无事可做；不管你多忙，他总是坚持要跟你去。

questions.q: How did Nigel answer Elizabeth's excuse about the dentist?
questions.zh: 奈杰尔是怎么回答她“去看牙医”的借口？
questions.a: 'Then I'll come with you,' he answered. 'There's always plenty to read in the waiting room!'
questions.aZh: “那我也跟你去，候诊室里总有很多东西可供阅读！”

questions.q: Why did Elizabeth's excuse fail, and what does the title 'Persistent' tell us about Nigel?
questions.zh: 借口为什么失败？标题揭示了奈杰尔的什么特点？
questions.a: Nigel is persistent: wherever she went he would come along, even to a dentist's waiting room. A vague excuse only invites him to join; she should have said plainly that she wanted to be alone.
questions.aZh: 奈杰尔锲而不舍：她去哪儿他都要跟着，连牙医候诊室也乐意去。含糊的借口反而给了他跟来的余地。

exercises.q: 动词填空：I crossed the street to avoid ______ (meet) him.
汉译英：再装作没看见他已经没有用了。（用 It was no use ...）
exercises.a: It was no use pretending that I had not seen him.
exercises.note: It is no use doing 固定句型。

exercises.q: 动词填空：I had to think of a way of preventing him from ______ (follow) me around all morning.
汉译英：不管你多忙，他总是坚持要跟你去。
exercises.a: No matter how busy you are, he always insists on coming with you.

exercises.q: 用所给词的适当形式填空：I never enjoy ______ (meet) Nigel Dykes. / Fancy ______ (meet) you here!
填空并说明 my 的作用：Would you mind my ______ (come) with you?
exercises.a: coming；my 是动名词 coming 的逻辑主语，也可用宾格 me。

exercises.q: 汉译英（反意疑问句）：你不忙，是吧？
exercises.a: You're not busy doing anything, are you?

quiz.q: “我穿过马路以便避开他”的正确英文是：
options: I crossed the street to avoid meeting him.
I crossed the street to avoid to meet him.
I crossed the street for avoid meeting him.
I crossed the street avoiding to meet him.

quiz.q: 下列哪一句中的动名词用法有错？
options: It was no use pretending that I had not seen him.
He always insists on coming with you.
I had to think of a way of preventing him from following me.
She avoided to meet him by crossing the street.
No matter how busy you are,
No matter how busy are you,
No matter what busy you are,
No matter how you are busy,
quiz.note: no matter + 疑问词，陈述语序。

quiz.q: 奈杰尔说 'Would you mind my coming with you?'，其中 my 的作用是：
options: the logical subject of 'coming'
the object of the verb 'mind'
a marker of the passive voice
modifying the word 'you'

quiz.q: “Fancy meeting you here!” 表达的意思是：
options: What a surprise to see you here!
Do you like meeting people here?
Please wait for me here.
I remember seeing you here.

quiz.q: 伊丽莎白说要去看牙医，奈杰尔的回答是：
options: 'Then I'll come with you. There's always plenty to read in the waiting room!'
'Then I'll wait for you outside the dentist's.'
'I'm sorry, but I have to leave now.'
'Would you mind my not coming with you?'
